section_title: Why is Edom’s claim to Israel’s land also a boast against the Lord?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 10 Because you have said, ‘These two nations and countries will be ours, and we will possess them,’ even though the LORD was there, 11 therefore as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will treat you according to the anger and jealousy you showed in your hatred against them, and I will make Myself known among them when I judge you. 12 Then you will know that I, the LORD, have heard every contemptuous word you uttered against the mountains of Israel when you said, ‘They are desolate; they are given to us to devour!’ 13 You boasted against Me with your mouth and multiplied your words against Me. I heard it Myself!

context_lines: Edom claims that the two nations and countries will become its possession. The Lord answers that He was there: the apparent opportunity is not a place outside His concern or authority.
He will deal with Edom according to the anger and jealousy shown in its hatred. What Edom has said about the mountains of Israel is heard by the Lord Himself.

The accusation moves from contempt for Israel’s ruined inheritance to arrogance against God. The people may imagine they are discussing unguarded land, but the Lord holds them accountable for their words and intentions.
common_interpretation_lines: [Wesley](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/ezekiel/35.htm) understands the Lord’s presence in relation to Israel. [Cambridge](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/cambridge/ezekiel/35.htm) identifies the two nations as Judah and Israel and connects the land with the Lord’s dwelling and claim upon it.

The [USCCB notes](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/ezekiel/35) likewise understand the hostile claim as an attack on the land’s sovereign. [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/ezekiel/35.htm) draws attention to the words God hears, including those spoken boldly as though no one could call the speaker to account.
